description:
Surfaced 2026-05-10 by PLINY during cleanup-bundle-2 ship (ariadne PR #34 / d83cd23). Two substrate-discipline observations from CATO's NEEDS-REVISIONS catch on the rxn helper that diff-only review would have missed.

## Observation 1: CATO empirical environment reproduction

CATO caught a load-bearing bug in rxn (_read_commit_from_dot_git silently failing inside git worktrees because .git is a file, not a directory) by RUNNING the helper against the live working tree, not just cold-reading the diff. The diff itself looked correct in isolation; only when CATO probed against the actual working environment did the gap surface.

This is a sharper shape than 'CATO cold-reads the diff for craft, hygiene, consistency, security, scope.' The substrate-canonical CATO discipline could include 'when the change interacts with environment state (filesystem, git internals, OS-specific behavior), CATO should empirically probe against the live working tree, not assume the diff is environment-agnostic.'

Substrate touch-point: substrate/CAPTAIN_CATO.md — add a brief discipline note in the review-method section about environment-interactive code patterns.

## Observation 2: Fallback-chain probe coverage

The rxn implementation has a multi-path fallback: env-var GIT_COMMIT → dot-git read → 'unknown' default. The initial probe set covered the env-var path (which silently passed even when dot-git was broken). The dot-git happy path had no independent probe.

Discipline implication: when a fallback chain has multiple resolution paths, ADA's probe set should cover each path independently. Otherwise one path's probes hide the others' bugs.

Substrate touch-point: substrate/MAJOR_PLINY.md — add a brief discipline note in ADA brief preamble template (or operating-disciplines.md probe-discipline section). Phrasing draft: 'When a code path uses fallback resolution (env-var → file → default), probes must independently exercise each resolution path. Probe coverage that hits only the env-var path will silently miss bugs in file-fallback paths.'

## Both observations have empirical anchor

Concrete instance: rxn _resolve_commit_sha() in PR #34 / d83cd23. Probe set initially had:
- env-var-set probe (PASS)
- env-var-unset path ASSUMED to exercise dot-git, but dot-git silently returned 'unknown' inside worktrees → fell through to default 'unknown' → probe still passed because 'unknown' was the assertion.

CATO's empirical reproduction caught it. Then ADA added a probe asserting dot-git happy path (returns actual SHA, not 'unknown') and the fix landed.

## Gauntlet

ADA + CATO eyeball. Substrate doc edits to substrate/CAPTAIN_CATO.md + substrate/MAJOR_PLINY.md (or op-disc, depending on placement). Small (~30-50 LOC). Skip DAEDALUS / ARGUS / VERA / ZENO.

## Sequencing

P3. Not blocking. Bundle into next stoa substrate-grooming dispatch. Both are real CATO/ADA discipline sharpenings; substrate value compounds across future engagements.

## Out of scope

- Generalizing 'environment-interactive review' beyond CATO's review method (separate concern; ARGUS may have analogous disciplines)
- Auto-detecting fallback-chain coverage gaps in ADA's probe authoring (way too ambitious)

## Empirical anchor

PLINY surface from cleanup-bundle-2 ship 2026-05-10 — CATO NEEDS-REVISIONS verdict on rxn revision round 1, then PASS after ADA addressed both findings.
title: CATO discipline refinements: empirical environment reproduction + fallback-chain probe coverage
